summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted for evaluation of intermittent sharp chest pain localized to the site of his implanted cardiac defibrillator. The pain resolved spontaneously and did not recur during hospitalization. Workup including EKG, serial troponins, and chest X-ray showed no evidence of acute cardiac ischemia, device malfunction, or infection. His chronic conditions—systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes, and CKD—were stable, with no medication changes made. He reported recent 20-pound weight loss attributed to improved fluid and dietary management. INR was subtherapeutic at 1.2, prompting outpatient follow-up. He was discharged home the following day with instructions to continue all home medications, monitor weight, and attend cardiology follow-up.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic neuropathy, unspecified
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
